subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In a broad sense, what is the meaning of 'Freedom' as related to the biblical accounts?
options: The right to commit crimes without punishment
Liberation from bondage, oppression, or slavery
Living on an island all by oneself
Refusing to obey any national laws
questions.explain: Biblical **freedom** generally refers to liberation, deliverance, or redemption from physical slavery, oppression, or spiritual bondage to sin.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of 'Spiritual Freedom'?
options: Being released from a physical prison cell
A country gaining independence from colonial rule
Being delivered from the bondage of sin and evil through Jesus Christ
Having the right to vote in an election
questions.explain: **Spiritual freedom** refers to being set free from the spiritual power of sin, death, and the devil, in contrast to political or physical freedom.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Exodus 3:1-15, God called Moses to lead the Israelites to freedom. Where was Moses keeping the flock of Jethro when God appeared to him?
options: Mount Carmel
Mount Horeb (the mountain of God)
Mount Zion
Mount Ararat
questions.explain: **Exodus 3:1** mentions that Moses led the flock to the west side of the wilderness and came to **Horeb, the mountain of God**.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: How did God visually manifest His presence to Moses when calling him to deliver Israel?
options: In a chariot of fire descending from the sky
Through a whirlwind carrying a loud trumpet
In a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush that was not consumed
Through a pillar of cloud hovering over a river
questions.explain: According to **Exodus 3:2**, the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a **flame of fire out of the midst of a bush**, and though the bush was burning, it was not consumed.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)

questions.q: When Moses approached the burning bush, what was the very first instruction God gave him? (Exodus 3:5)
options: To take off his sandals because the ground was holy
To immediately pack his bags and go to Egypt
To write down everything he heard on stone tablets
To wash his face in the nearby stream
questions.explain: **Exodus 3:5** says: 'Then he said, “Do not come near; **take your sandals off your feet**, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.”'

questions.q: In Judges 4, which female prophetess and judge did God use to call the people of Israel to freedom from Jabin, king of Canaan?
options: Esther
Ruth
Deborah
Miriam
questions.explain: **Deborah**, a prophetess and the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time (Judges 4:4) and she initiated the military campaign to win their freedom.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Who was the military commander that Deborah called and ordered to lead the Israelite army into battle for their freedom?
options: Gideon
Samson
Barak
Joshua
questions.explain: According to **Judges 4:6**, Deborah summoned **Barak** the son of Abinoam and gave him the command from the Lord to gather his men and march to Mount Tabor to fight.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Judges 4, when Deborah delivered God's command to Barak to lead the army against their oppressors, what was Barak's condition for going to the battle?
options: He demanded half of the kingdom's wealth.
He insisted that he be crowned king first.
He said he would only go if Deborah went with him.
He asked for an extra ten thousand men from Egypt.
questions.explain: In **Judges 4:8**, Barak said to Deborah, 'If you will go with me, I will go, but if you will not go with me, I will not go.'
